idiom_name: struct envelope with a Type field + handler map (or type switch) over a channel
implementation_notes: Go has no command class hierarchy to collapse: the classic structure reduces to a struct with a discriminator field plus encoding/json tags for the wire form, and dispatch is a map[string]func or a type switch on the decoded payload - a handler registry keyed by the type string keeps the receiver closed for modification. In-process command buses send the struct on chan Command with a select loop; distributed ones publish the same struct with a broker client (NATS, Kafka, AMQP) and the discriminator travels in the payload. Nothing here requires a framework, which is why this is idiomatic rather than library.
pitfalls: json.RawMessage defers decoding to the handler, so a misspelled or unknown type tag fails at the lookup step - return an explicit error instead of indexing a nil function.
Interface values and type switches trade compile-time exhaustiveness for runtime defaults: adding a command without a handler is a silent no-op unless the default branch fails loudly.

An unbuffered or unbounded command channel breaks the guarantee the broker would give: a full channel blocks the sender (or a goroutine), and a dropped context removes cancellation from queued commands.
